checks.text: With the default 2x2 matrices A = [[1,2],[3,4]] and B = [[5,6],[7,8]] and the operation select set to "Add", the result table shows 6, 8, 10, 12 in the cells at (row 1, col 1), (1, 2), (2, 1), (2, 2).

Changing the operation select to "Multiply" with the same default matrices shows 19, 22, 43, 50 in the result cells (1,1), (1,2), (2,1), (2,2). (1*5+2*7 = 19, 1*6+2*8 = 22, 3*5+4*7 = 43, 3*6+4*8 = 50.)
With the operation "Add" and default matrices, clicking the button "Copy result" puts exactly the text "6 8 10 12" on the clipboard.

Selecting "3x3" in the select labelled "Both sizes" (it starts at "2x2") shows three rows and three columns of inputs in both matrices (inputs "A11".."A33" and "B11".."B33") and resets every matrix cell to 0, so the result table (operation "Add") is a 3x3 grid in which every cell is 0.
With operation "Add" and the default matrices, changing cell "A11" from 1 to 9 changes result cell (1,1) from 6 to 14; clicking the button "Undo" restores "A11" to 1 and result cell (1,1) to 6.
After selecting "Multiply" and changing "A11" to 10, reloading the page shows the operation select set to "Multiply" and the input "A11" with the value 10.

With operation "Multiply", leaving A at 2x2 and selecting "3x3" in the select labelled "Size B" (A stays 2x2) makes the result area show the message "Dimensions do not match for multiplication" (columns of A = 2, rows of B = 3).
